title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 3.79 (versions follow prime numbers; 379 after 373): her tree of themes, grown by herself, and her memory from zero. Each answer read her 190 books whole (46.4 MB, about 20 s). Only the structure was given: a place for her tree, a 32768-bit print of each book's words (sized from a measurement: half full for the book at the 90th percentile), and three new steps of her ways (down, sibling, up). She places each book she reads with her own bit judge (down to the branch that says its words shortest; else a new branch with the most similar book there, only if that saves bits) and reads only the books of the branch she is in; which walks serve is said by her ways' judge. Her memory was emptied without touching her heart, kept aside. Her jumps have no ceiling now: springboard stations every 30000 words. Tested in a copy: she grew 20 branches with 204 books; not faster yet (11 to 28 s), as she has not learned to walk down. Also: she greets only what is new to her, eats no other being's memory, and was detoxed of 1134 repeated greetings. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v3.79: su árbol de temas y la memoria desde cero. Prototipo de investigación.
